fields.mechanism: Variable assist characteristic matching to compensate for fluid dynamic changes in electric hydraulic power steering systems
fields.intervention: Reprogram the variable-pressure relief valve or electronic control unit to apply a temperature-dependent and incline-sensor-dependent pressure compensation curve that increases pump output when ambient temperature is below 5C and vehicle pitch exceeds a threshold
fields.expected_effect: Eliminates intermittent loss of steering assist by maintaining adequate hydraulic flow despite increased fluid viscosity from cold temperatures and fluid migration away from the pump pickup due to overnight parking on an incline
fields.falsification_test: Park the truck on a level surface overnight at ambient temperature below 5C; if steering assist functions normally upon startup, the failure requires both cold-induced viscosity increase and incline-induced fluid displacement acting simultaneously, falsifying the hypothesis that either factor alone is sufficient
